neighbours.label: the word after an ability/expertise verb (can tell a, knows how to, could sniff out): skill at judging or doing something
fire: My grandmother could spot a counterfeit banknote from across the room.
A good sommelier can tell a cheap wine just by the smell of the cork.
Our old coach really knew how to motivate a tired team at halftime.
That detective could read a liar's face like an open book.
Only a seasoned trader can sense a market crash before it happens.
The best chefs know how to balance salt and acid without tasting twice.
As a teacher she could hold a restless classroom's attention for an hour.
A true carpenter can judge a plank's strength by tapping it once.
quiet: My grandmother kept a counterfeit banknote in a drawer for years.
A good sommelier bought a cheap wine for the staff party last week.
Our old coach drove a tired team home after the long tournament.
That detective wrote a long report about the robbery downtown.
Only a seasoned trader works on the top floor of the old bank.
The best chefs in town buy their salt from the same small shop.
As a teacher she rented a small flat near the school for an hour's walk.
A true carpenter stored a plank of oak in the shed behind the house.
